dataset.datasetnotes:
Description of sampling from Davis et al 1994 CJFAS, p. 1856:  
"Most of the lakes were sampled three times in 1983 and four times in 1984, during the ice-free seasons, and in accord with protocols of the Paleoecological Investigation of Recent Lake Acidification (PIRLA) 
(Charles and Whitehead 1986;Norton et al. 1986). Fourteen of the lakes in New Hampshire and Vermont were sampled only in 1984. For some lakes,
occasional non-PIRLA data from 1978 to 1980 (Norton et al.1981) and from 1988 to 1984 (Buso et al. 1984; Haines et al. 1984; Kahl et al. 1985) were added. The non-PIRLA data were collected in accord with USEPA protocols and, like the PIRLA data, were subjected to rigorous quality control and assurance."

From Charles and Whitehead 1986, p. 16-19, N NE Water Chemistry methods:
"All sampling was conducted where the water depth was at least 90 percent of maximum.  A YSI O2 temperature meter and probe were used to establish the depth of stratified water (top of metalimnion), if present.  Only the mixed part of the water column was sampled, using a 9 mm I.D. flexible Tygon tube to a maximum depth of 2 m above the sediment.  
Water column samples were taken from a minimum of five different locations over the deepest part of the lake and combined in a four liter linear polyethelene (LPE) collection bottle.  At remote lakes less than three meters deep, samples were taken by hand dipping directly into sample bottles from approximately 0.5 m depth."

Sample collections were made by various combinations of the project investigators, helped by field assistants.
This dataset was originally uploaded to the Academy of Natural Sciences of Drexel University constituent database, which was merged into the Diatom Paleolimnology Data Cooperative (DPDC) constituent database in July 2026.
